_comment: Keyed by framework name so a different standards set (e.g. a state's own framework) can be swapped in or added later without changing the shape consumers rely on. Each standard's 'paraphrase' is an original one-line restatement, not the verbatim standard text, per the Common Core Public License (see frameworks.CCSS-M.license below). Audited coverage so far is Algebra 1 only — see CURRICULUM_AUDIT.md.

CCSS-M.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics
CCSS-M.scope: High School: Number and Quantity (N), Algebra (A), Functions (F), Statistics and Probability (S)
CCSS-M.attribution: © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.
CCSS-M.license: Per the Common Core public license (thecorestandards.org/public-license/): the standards may be copied, published, distributed, and displayed for purposes that support the Common Core State Standards Initiative, with the attribution notice above included (states that have fully adopted the standards are exempt from that requirement). Verbatim standard text is NOT reproduced here — each entry below is an original paraphrase, which is the more conservative choice beyond what the license strictly requires.
CCSS-M.plusStandardNote: Standards marked plus:true carry the official '(+)' designation — content intended for students pursuing advanced/STEM math pathways, generally beyond a first Algebra 1 course (more typically Algebra 2, Precalculus, or a 4th-year course).

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Real Number System
standards.paraphrase: Explains why rational exponents are a natural extension of integer-exponent rules, and connects that notation to radicals.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Real Number System
standards.paraphrase: Rewrites expressions that mix radicals and rational exponents using the laws of exponents.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Real Number System
standards.paraphrase: Explains, in general, which combinations of rational and irrational numbers under addition/multiplication stay rational and which become irrational.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Chooses and interprets units and scale consistently when setting up and solving multi-step real-world problems and graphs.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Defines the quantities a descriptive model needs, as part of setting the model up.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Chooses a sensible level of precision for a reported measurement given how it was measured.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
standards.paraphrase: States that i satisfies i^2 = -1 and that every complex number can be written a + bi.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
standards.paraphrase: Adds, subtracts, and multiplies complex numbers using i^2 = -1 together with the usual number properties.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
standards.paraphrase: Uses the conjugate of a complex number to find moduli and quotients.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
standards.paraphrase: Plots complex numbers in rectangular and polar form and shows both describe the same number.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
standards.paraphrase: Carries out complex-number operations geometrically on the complex plane.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
standards.paraphrase: Finds distance and midpoint between two numbers in the complex plane.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
standards.paraphrase: Solves quadratic equations that have complex (non-real) solutions.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
standards.paraphrase: Extends polynomial identities to work over the complex numbers.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
standards.paraphrase: States the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra and confirms it for quadratics.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Represents a vector quantity (magnitude + direction) as a directed segment with proper notation.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Finds a vector's components from its initial and terminal points.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Uses vectors to solve problems involving velocity and similar directional quantities.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Adds and subtracts vectors.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Multiplies a vector by a scalar.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Uses a matrix to organize and represent data such as a network or payoff table.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Multiplies a matrix by a scalar.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Adds, subtracts, and multiplies matrices of compatible sizes.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Recognizes that matrix multiplication is associative/distributive but not commutative.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Identifies the role of the zero and identity matrices, analogous to 0 and 1.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Uses a matrix to transform a vector, treating the vector as a one-column matrix.

standards.domain: Number and Quantity — Vector and Matrix Quantities
standards.paraphrase: Uses a 2x2 matrix as a plane transformation and ties its determinant to an area scale factor.

standards.domain: Algebra — Seeing Structure in Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Interprets the parts of an expression (terms, factors, coefficients) in terms of what they mean in context.

standards.domain: Algebra — Seeing Structure in Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Spots structural patterns in an expression that suggest a useful way to rewrite it.

standards.domain: Algebra — Seeing Structure in Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Rewrites an expression into an equivalent, more useful form (e.g. factored) to reveal a property it has.

standards.domain: Algebra — Seeing Structure in Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Derives and applies the finite geometric series sum formula.

standards.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Adds, subtracts, and multiplies polynomials, understanding they behave like a closed number system similar to the integers.

standards.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Applies the Remainder Theorem to relate a polynomial's value at a to its remainder when divided by (x - a).

standards.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Uses known factors of a polynomial to find its zeros and sketch its graph.

standards.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Proves and uses polynomial identities (e.g. the difference-of-squares pattern) to describe numeric relationships.

standards.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Applies the Binomial Theorem to expand (x + y)^n.

standards.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Rewrites a rational expression in the form quotient + remainder/divisor.

standards.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions
standards.paraphrase: Treats rational expressions as a closed system under the four operations, like rational numbers.

standards.domain: Algebra — Creating Equations
standards.paraphrase: Writes a one-variable equation or inequality (linear or quadratic) to model a problem and solves it.

standards.domain: Algebra — Creating Equations
standards.paraphrase: Writes a two-variable equation to represent a relationship and graphs it with labeled, scaled axes.

standards.domain: Algebra — Creating Equations
standards.paraphrase: Models real constraints with equations/inequalities (often a system) and judges whether a solution actually makes sense in context.

standards.domain: Algebra — Creating Equations
standards.paraphrase: Rearranges a formula to isolate a different variable of interest, using the same moves as solving an equation.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Justifies each step of solving an equation as a consequence of the previous, equal step.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Solves simple rational/radical equations in one variable and checks for extraneous solutions.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Solves linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including with literal (letter) coefficients.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Solves one-variable quadratic equations by an appropriate method (factoring, completing the square, or the quadratic formula).

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Shows that replacing one equation in a system with a combination of the two preserves the same solution set — the logic behind elimination.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Solves systems of linear equations exactly and by graphing.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Solves a linear-and-quadratic system in two variables algebraically and graphically.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Represents a linear system as a single matrix equation.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Uses a matrix inverse to solve a linear system.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Understands a two-variable equation's graph as the set of every ordered pair that satisfies it.

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Explains why the intersection of y = f(x) and y = g(x) gives the solutions of f(x) = g(x).

standards.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations & Inequalities
standards.paraphrase: Graphs a two-variable linear inequality (and a system of them) as a shaded half-plane region.

standards.domain: Functions — Interpreting Functions
standards.paraphrase: Defines a function as a rule assigning exactly one output to each input.

standards.domain: Functions — Interpreting Functions
standards.paraphrase: Uses function notation and evaluates/interprets a function at specific inputs in context.

standards.domain: Functions — Interpreting Functions
standards.paraphrase: Recognizes a sequence as a function on a subset of the integers, sometimes defined recursively.

standards.domain: Functions — Interpreting Functions
standards.paraphrase: Reads and sketches key features (intercepts, max/min, increasing/decreasing) of a function modeling a real relationship.

standards.domain: Functions — Interpreting Functions
standards.paraphrase: Connects a function's domain to what its graph shows and what makes sense in context.

standards.domain: Functions — Interpreting Functions
standards.paraphrase: Calculates and interprets a function's average rate of change over an interval.

standards.domain: Functions — Interpreting Functions
standards.paraphrase: Graphs a function from its symbolic form, showing its key features.

standards.domain: Functions — Interpreting Functions
standards.paraphrase: Rewrites a function's expression in an equivalent form to expose a different property of it.

standards.domain: Functions — Interpreting Functions
standards.paraphrase: Compares properties of two functions given in different representations (equation, graph, table, description).

standards.domain: Functions — Building Functions
standards.paraphrase: Writes a function to model a relationship between two quantities.

standards.domain: Functions — Building Functions
standards.paraphrase: Writes arithmetic/geometric sequences both recursively and explicitly, and translates between the two.

standards.domain: Functions — Building Functions
standards.paraphrase: Predicts how f(x)+k, k·f(x), f(kx), or f(x+k) transforms a graph, and finds k from a graph.

standards.domain: Functions — Building Functions
standards.paraphrase: Finds the inverse of a function.

standards.domain: Functions — Building Functions
standards.paraphrase: Uses the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms to solve problems with either.

standards.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, & Exponential Models
standards.paraphrase: Distinguishes situations that grow linearly from ones that grow exponentially.

standards.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, & Exponential Models
standards.paraphrase: Builds a linear or exponential function from a graph, description, or two input-output pairs.

standards.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, & Exponential Models
standards.paraphrase: Shows, using graphs/tables, that exponential growth eventually overtakes linear, quadratic, or polynomial growth.

standards.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, & Exponential Models
standards.paraphrase: Expresses the solution to an exponential model as a logarithm.

standards.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, & Exponential Models
standards.paraphrase: Interprets what the parameters of a linear or exponential model mean in context (e.g. starting value, growth factor).

standards.domain: Functions — Trigonometric Functions
standards.paraphrase: Defines radian measure as an arc length on the unit circle.

standards.domain: Functions — Trigonometric Functions
standards.paraphrase: Extends trig functions to all real numbers using the unit circle.

standards.domain: Functions — Trigonometric Functions
standards.paraphrase: Derives exact trig values for common reference angles using special triangles and the unit circle.

standards.domain: Functions — Trigonometric Functions
standards.paraphrase: Uses the unit circle to explain trig functions' symmetry and periodicity.

standards.domain: Functions — Trigonometric Functions
standards.paraphrase: Chooses a trig function to model periodic behavior with given amplitude, frequency, and midline.

standards.domain: Functions — Trigonometric Functions
standards.paraphrase: Restricts a trig function's domain so its inverse can be defined.

standards.domain: Functions — Trigonometric Functions
standards.paraphrase: Uses inverse trig functions to solve equations from modeling contexts.

standards.domain: Functions — Trigonometric Functions
standards.paraphrase: Proves and applies the Pythagorean trig identity sin^2 + cos^2 = 1.

standards.domain: Functions — Trigonometric Functions
standards.paraphrase: Proves and applies the angle sum/difference formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
standards.paraphrase: Represents one-variable data with dot plots, histograms, or box plots.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
standards.paraphrase: Compares the center and spread of two or more data sets using measures suited to their shape.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
standards.paraphrase: Interprets differences in shape, center, and spread between data sets, accounting for outliers.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
standards.paraphrase: Fits data to a normal distribution using mean/standard deviation and knows when that's inappropriate.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
standards.paraphrase: Summarizes two-category data in a two-way table and interprets relative frequencies.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
standards.paraphrase: Plots two quantitative variables on a scatter plot and describes their relationship.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
standards.paraphrase: Interprets a linear model's slope and intercept in context.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
standards.paraphrase: Computes and interprets a correlation coefficient for a linear fit.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
standards.paraphrase: Distinguishes correlation from causation.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
standards.paraphrase: Understands statistics as inferring population parameters from a random sample.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
standards.paraphrase: Checks whether a proposed model is consistent with observed data, e.g. via simulation.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
standards.paraphrase: Distinguishes surveys, experiments, and observational studies, and explains the role of randomization in each.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
standards.paraphrase: Estimates a population mean/proportion from sample data and a simulation-based margin of error.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
standards.paraphrase: Uses simulation from a randomized experiment to judge whether a treatment difference is significant.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
standards.paraphrase: Critically evaluates a data-based report.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
standards.paraphrase: Describes events as subsets of a sample space, including unions, intersections, and complements.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
standards.paraphrase: Defines independence of two events via P(A and B) = P(A)P(B).

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
standards.paraphrase: Defines conditional probability and connects it to independence.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
standards.paraphrase: Builds a two-way frequency table and uses it to judge independence or estimate conditional probabilities.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
standards.paraphrase: Explains conditional probability and independence in everyday terms.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
standards.paraphrase: Computes a conditional probability as a fraction of outcomes and interprets it in context.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
standards.paraphrase: Applies the Addition Rule for P(A or B).

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
standards.paraphrase: Applies the general Multiplication Rule for P(A and B).

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
standards.paraphrase: Uses permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Using Probability to Make Decisions
standards.paraphrase: Defines a random variable over a sample space and graphs its probability distribution.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Using Probability to Make Decisions
standards.paraphrase: Calculates and interprets a random variable's expected value.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Using Probability to Make Decisions
standards.paraphrase: Builds a theoretical probability distribution and finds its expected value.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Using Probability to Make Decisions
standards.paraphrase: Builds an empirical probability distribution and finds its expected value.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Using Probability to Make Decisions
standards.paraphrase: Weighs decision outcomes by assigning probabilities and payoffs to find expected value.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Using Probability to Make Decisions
standards.paraphrase: Uses probability to make a fair decision.

standards.domain: Statistics & Probability — Using Probability to Make Decisions
standards.paraphrase: Analyzes a real decision or strategy using probability concepts.
